A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CP2 framework and its HPD and PCP variants. The main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture simulations and experiments on nine regression datasets, including coverage, prediction-set sizes, clustering and UMAP analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original simulation and regression results and adds experiments on six multi-target datasets, including coverage and projected prediction-set areas.

M1.justification: v2 Appendix B.1 corrects the reported HPD conformity score from density to negative density, with corresponding negative thresholds so the nested sets increase with their parameter. The general CP2 calibration and two-sample CP2-PCP procedure remain; specialized pseudocode and multidimensional evaluation do not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Section 4.3 adds multi-target regression on rf1, rf2, scm1d, scm20d, indoor and sgemm_small, covering river flow, supply chains, localization and GPU computation time. The nine scalar-response datasets and Gaussian-mixture experiment are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Table 3 omits the CP2-HYB-D and CP2-HYB-L comparisons reported alongside PCP variants in v1 Table 4. The external comparator set remains CP, PCP, the unconformalized conditional model, CHR, CQR and CQR2; CHR was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The new multidimensional experiments introduce coordinatewise Bonferroni adjustment for scalar methods, 1000 generative samples, and grid-based projected-area measurements and rankings. sgemm_small uses 10000-example subsamples, and its area comparison standardizes targets. These are new evaluation protocols, not established changes to the retained scalar experiments.

E4.justification: v2 removes the worst-slab sensitivity comparison at a 0.4 minimum slab fraction shown in v1 Figure 8. It adds a qualitative report that exponential, sigmoid and tanh adjustments performed worse than linear and additive adjustments. The clustering and UMAP analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies 10 replications for the projected-area ranking experiment in Figure 8. The existing 50-split reporting practice is retained, including for the new multidimensional coverage plots; no increase in repetitions for existing experiments or new significance-testing practice is established.

E6.justification: v2 adds multidimensional coverage and size results in Figures 6–8 and Table 4. For example, sgemm_small's axes (0, 1) have mean projected areas of 0.435 for PCP, 0.576 for CP2-PCP-L and 0.560 for CP2-PCP-D. These are new results, not same-setting improvements. All 216 retained scalar-result entries in v2 Table 3 match v1 Table 4 after column alignment.

T1.justification: v2 adds consistency assumption H3 and Theorem 3.3, giving a conditional-coverage error rate of O_P(sqrt(log(n)/n) + r_n), beyond v1's oracle-based asymptotic discussion. Appendices A.2–A.4 add upper coverage bounds, deviation bounds and supporting proofs, while H1 is revised. The earlier alternative-quantile corollary survives as Corollary A.11.

C1.justification: v2's contributions explicitly claim asymptotic conditional validity under predictive-distribution consistency and emphasize multidimensional prediction and its empirical validation. This materially extends the principal theoretical and application claims beyond v1's approximate-validity contribution and scalar experimental emphasis.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of Bonferroni-induced overcoverage, PCP's prediction-size versus conditional-coverage tradeoff, and the computational difficulty of high-dimensional HPD regions. It removes v1 Appendix C's explicit binning-compatibility caution, while retaining the central dependence on conditional-distribution estimation quality.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix B.3 first documents using 25% of data to select a worst slab, 75% to evaluate it, and 5000 shared random directions. Table 2 specifies reference values for the adjustment functions, and specialized algorithms expand implementation guidance. The Brent-solver statement disappears; network architectures, training budgets and implementation links remain.

R1.justification: Much related work is retained and relocated. v2 additionally credits Deutschmann et al. for score transformations, adds references supporting density consistency, generative models and multidimensional datasets, and sharpens its positioning against fixed-radius PCP. Some earlier discussions, including Rossellini et al., are omitted.

P1.justification: The introduction, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work moves into the introduction, HPD moves to Appendix B.1, asymptotics are integrated into the theory section, and Appendix C disappears. The title, author list and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening illustrations with a funnel example, removes the CP2 schematic and parameter illustration, and adds three multidimensional plots and an area table. It removes the 0.4-slab plot, narrows and reorganizes the scalar table, redesigns the adjustment-function table, and replaces the paired generic algorithm displays with specialized pseudocode.

improvement.justification: v1's asymptotic discussion assumes an oracle distribution, and its experiments test scalar responses. v2 adds consistency-based theoretical support and evaluates multidimensional coverage and size tradeoffs on six datasets, addressing important gaps in support for the framework. These gains outweigh the loss of the 0.4-slab sensitivity comparison and the explicit binning-compatibility caution.
